label: the crawler (models/headcrab.mdl): a sludge crawler: low, wet, six-legged, the size of a headcrab, grey-green with a pale belly and a ring of teeth

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/roach.mdl, models/leech.mdl, models/chumtoad.mdl: the judge does not know which
measured.contract: keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts

M1.reason: The outline is a plain rectangular block (sides.png, all ten views). The brief asks for a low, wet, six-legged crawler with a ring of teeth, and none of that silhouette is there: no legs, no head, no teeth. Front-left and back-right show only a cuboid.

M2.reason: The measured size is 12 x 10 x 6 units, but sizeAsked is null, so there is no number to check it against. The brief only says 'the size of a headcrab'. The footprint is roughly headcrab-scale, but it is not verified against a brief figure.

M3.reason: Missing: no six legs, no ring of teeth, no head, no pale belly region. The model is one solid box, and the 'below' view shows a flat dark face where a belly should be.

M4.reason: The whole body is one flat mid-grey (lineup C, sides.png). The brief asks for grey-green with a pale belly; the hue is off and the belly is dark grey, not pale. The grey is at least a plausible wet-stone tone, so it is clearly off rather than absent.

M5.reason: No surface detail of the crawler is there: no wet sheen, no teeth, no wear or markings. The only texture is a faint mottled noise across every face, which is not the crawler's surface.

M6.reason: In lineup.png the box is panel C, beside the three Half-Life creatures and a dart-like prop. A player would take it for a block, not a Half-Life creature. The line-up shows what it is at a glance.

M7.reason: A box has no identifiable front, so the front cannot be the crawler's front. It stands on its base, but there is nothing to place as a creature facing a direction.

M8.reason: The SMAK check reports no errors (checkErrors empty). Twelve triangles is well under the cap for a prop of this size. The box is closed, with no open, inside-out or floating faces.

C1.reason: In run.png (walk 0 to 34) the block slides and bobs along the floor line without coming apart. In attack.png (jump 0 to 30) it tumbles end over end as one rigid box. There are no legs moving, so it does not move as a six-legged crawler does. Nothing detaches, but the motion is clearly not the original's.

C2.reason: The measured contract line says the model keeps the headcrab's bones, animations, attachments and bodyparts, so no fault is recorded. This is the one item the measurement supports as a full pass, and it does not change the verdict on the shape.
